- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 92+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to reflect this, often holding high values.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values are trending lower.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late, missing the immediate drop.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” after a sharp decline; tends to underestimate the magnitude of recovery.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often overcorrects upward in the short term, then undercorrects later.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent high values — model tends to “climb” with recent peaks, even if they are unsustainable.
- Model underestimates the impact of consecutive low values — fails to recognize that a low price can persist longer than expected.
- Model often ignores the “tail risk” of sudden drops — underestimates the probability of sharp downward corrections.
